core_obligations: Show that the base change condition implies the representable sense immediately by testing with Z a scheme (proof lines 11112-11117).
Conversely, from the representable sense deduce that X -> Y is integral, universally injective and surjective (proof lines 11118-11124).
Apply that an integral morphism is universally closed (proof lines 11125-11126).
Combine universal closedness with universal injectivity and surjectivity to conclude the homeomorphism property for every base change (proof lines 11127-11128).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma: a representable morphism f : X -> Y of algebraic spaces over S is a universal homeomorphism in the representable sense if and only if every base change Z x_Y X -> Z induces a homeomorphism of the underlying topological spaces (source lines 11100-11109). One direction is formal from the definition. The other uses the structure of universal homeomorphisms: from the representable sense one gets that X -> Y is integral, universally injective and surjective, hence universally closed by the integral morphism statement, so combining universal closedness, universal injectivity and surjectivity gives the homeomorphism property after every base change.
